title: PISCO · 一扇帘，六种夜晚
status: 完整24镜分镜；实际视频状态见各场生产记录
quotePolicy: 六句英文 quote 逐字保留原文；分支选项与结果同步当前网站 stories.json，按 v9 画面修正动作与道具。

interactionContract.forward: 滚动、触控滑动或方向键控制镜头推进；先看清角色行动，再接近自然存在的道具。
interactionContract.backward: 可按同一轨道回退，复看人物动作、道具近景和上一世界，保持空间方向。
interactionContract.hold: 停手即停留，不限时、不自动替用户选剧情；人物邀请完成处保留阅读窗口。
interactionContract.cta: 入站先给 Step inside；各场邀请完成后出现该场 CTA 和原对白；结尾提供故事选项与六世界回访。

transitionContract.method: 推进至实际尾帧道具 → 短匹配溶解到共享微距 → 匹配下一场入镜道具 / 环境 → 拉开新世界
transitionContract.truth: 共享近景与实际 end 图不是像素一致裁片，不能硬称无缝。需在轮廓、位置、明度与运动上做匹配，并以短溶解或补拍近景桥接。
transitionContract.videoTruth: 七段 TapNow · Hailuo 02 实际视频均已取回，可在本页播放。已检查人物身份、不同动作和首尾衔接；网站已接入全部七段视频，道具推进由同一条可逆镜头轨道控制。每段约6秒，串联观看规划约60秒。

transitions.name: 蕾丝面具 → 床边面具
transitions.match: 同一只眼孔的杏仁轮廓、细银边、象牙蕾丝与暗部深度
transitions.entry: 拉开成吸血鬼床边桌上的完整面具，再显露身后的斜卧角色。
transitions.bridge: 先推到会所面具的左眼孔；接共享微距后，用短匹配溶解接床边面具，再拉开场景。
transitions.avoid: 不要把面具举到镜头前；不要将双眼面具替换成金色单眼牌。

transitions.name: 窗中圆月 → 乳白球灯
transitions.match: 圆形边界、珍珠白明度与由暗到亮的中心
transitions.entry: 从球灯外轮廓拉开，露出海边会客空间与三人各自的动作。
transitions.bridge: 邀请结束后才抬升推向窗中圆月；在共享白色圆盘近景匹配圆心与大小，再短溶解成球灯。
transitions.avoid: 不要突然出现光门；不要在圆形尚未填满视线时硬切另一间房。

transitions.name: 玄关头盔 → 车把旁头盔
transitions.match: 黑色弧形镜片边界与一条弯曲琥珀反光
transitions.entry: 从同类镜片拉开，看见头盔已自然挂在车把旁，骑手正准备上车。
transitions.bridge: 镜头接近凳上的镜片；在黑色镜面与弧光特写中短匹配溶解，接车库头盔。
transitions.avoid: 头盔始终有真实支撑点；人物不向镜头递头盔。

transitions.name: 固定后视镜 → 月下林径
transitions.match: 镜中居中的湿石小径、拱形树冠与三点灯位（中间更高）
transitions.entry: 越过圆镜边缘后，林径直接成为全画幅，女王在前方回望。
transitions.bridge: 拍完空后座后推向仍固定在支架上的圆镜；共享镜面近景中短匹配溶解，再接女王林径首帧。
transitions.avoid: 镜子不脱离支架、不忽然放大成手持道具；花园里不再出现一面凭空的镜子。

transitions.name: 地图边单烛 → 餐桌前烛火
transitions.match: 细长火焰的尖端、暖黄白焰心与竖直运动方向
transitions.entry: 从火焰拉开，露出晚餐桌、空椅及准备第三份晚餐的两人。
transitions.bridge: 摘冠与护火动作先完整结束；随后推近火焰，短匹配溶解到室友前景烛火，再拉开晚餐。
transitions.avoid: 不要让她把蜡烛拿到镜头前；室友画面只保留一根主烛。

scenes.lead: He draws the burgundy curtain aside. Beyond the last dance, a twenty-eight-year-old stranger has saved a quieter corner for you.
ends: You rest your hand beside his mask. “Tell me what you were hoping I would say.” His teasing expression softens.
He admits that he spent the evening inventing reasons to find you. You tell him he could have simply asked for your company.
He moves to the other end of the sofa, leaving you room. The conversation becomes easier once neither of you has to perform.
The gala ends behind the glass. Here, your evening is beginning with an invitation you can answer for yourself.
You nod toward the covered terrace. He offers his hand, and you take it when you are ready.
Under the awning, the rain quiets the city. You tell him what you enjoyed about the evening and what you would rather leave behind.
He listens, then asks a simpler question: “Would you like to see me again?” You watch the lights reflected in his glass.
You have the whole walk back to decide what comes next. He is happy to match your pace.

scenes.lead: Beyond the masquerade lies a moonlit room. A silver-haired vampire, with the appearance of a twenty-eight-year-old man, makes room beside him.
ends: “Stay and keep me company,” you say. He nods, letting you decide what the invitation means.
You settle by the open window with a blanket and two cups of tea. He asks which part of the evening you wish had lasted longer.
You trade small, true stories until the music downstairs fades. When you grow quiet, he asks whether you would like him to stay.
Dawn is still hours away. For once, neither of you is in a hurry to make the night into anything more than this.
You point toward the moonlit path below. He offers you his arm and lets you choose the way.
The castle grows smaller behind you. He tells you which trees flower at night, and you tell him why you came to the ball.
At a stone bridge, you stop to listen to the water. He asks what would make you return, then waits without trying to answer for you.
The path bends back toward the castle. You can keep walking, or turn this shared silence into the beginning of another conversation.

scenes.lead: Three college housemates, all twenty-one or older, have cleared an evening for you in their seaside athlete house.
ends: You settle beside the dark-haired athlete. The others accept your choice with a smile and return to the kitchen.
He tells you about a match he still thinks about. You ask what he loves about the game when nobody is watching.
His answer has little to do with winning. You trade stories while the sea outside becomes a dark line under the sky.
He asks whether you would like to walk down to the shore. The next part of the evening is yours to choose together.
You turn toward the silver-haired housemate beside the entry bench. His bright smile softens as he asks what you feel like doing.
You choose the balcony. He brings two drinks and admits he rehearsed several impressive ways to welcome you.
You ask him to try a simple hello instead. He does, and you both laugh at how much easier the conversation becomes.
The kitchen lights glow behind you. Out here, a playful introduction is becoming a reason to stay.
You join the blond housemate at the counter. He sets your drink within reach and asks if you would like a quieter corner.
You sit by the window, sharing the last of the sunset. He asks about the thing you have been most excited to tell someone.
He listens closely, then offers a story of his own. The house settles around you while the conversation keeps finding new paths.
When the others call that dinner is ready, he waits for your answer. You can join them now, or finish this thought together.

scenes.lead: At twenty-seven, he knows every late-night corner of the city. Tonight, he wants to know which one you would choose.
ends: You ask for somewhere neither of you has been. He laughs and asks what you would like to find, keeping the motorcycle parked while you decide.
You suggest a tiny all-night café neither of you has tried. You make a plan over the sound of rain, discovering how differently you each choose a route.
When the weather clears, he takes the spare helmet from its hook and checks that it fits. You tell him you would like to take the slow way.
The garage door opens onto a quiet street. The destination is simple; getting to know each other is the adventure.
“Right here sounds good,” you say. He switches off the work light and pulls two chairs into the warmer glow by the doorway.
With the motorcycle safely parked, he brings hot drinks. You ask what he usually thinks about when the city finally becomes quiet.
The answer turns into a story, then another. Your hand finds his only after he offers it across the space between your chairs.
The rain begins to ease, but neither of you moves immediately. You can leave whenever you like; staying has become a choice of its own.

scenes.lead: The adult elven queen has dismissed the court. In her secluded garden, she asks you to meet the woman behind the crown.
ends: You say her name without the title. Her shoulders ease, and the smile that follows belongs only to this quiet garden.
She asks how your day really went. You tell her a small story from the city that never found its way into a council report.
Together, you trace a route across the open map. She asks whether you would show her that place someday.
Beyond the arches, the city is still awake. Beside the map, a promise begins with a name and the freedom to answer honestly.
You ask what she wants you to know now that the crown rests on the map table. She considers the question, then makes room for you beside her.
She speaks about a garden she misses and a song she has forgotten. You share a memory that has stayed with you just as quietly.
The maps remain open, but the conversation has moved beyond borders. She asks whether you would return simply to talk.
You answer in your own time. For tonight, being heard is enough to make the garden feel different.

scenes.lead: Your two adult roommates, twenty and twenty-two, have saved dinner for you. Tonight, a familiar welcome carries a new possibility.
ends: You turn toward your auburn-haired roommate by the empty chair and ask if she would like to take a walk after dinner. She smiles and says yes.
Your other roommate wishes you both a good evening. You make sure the choice feels comfortable for everyone before making plans.
On the quiet street, you talk about when familiar company started to feel like something more. Neither of you needs a perfect answer.
The apartment lights remain warm above you. You have room to discover this new possibility at a pace you both enjoy.
You ask your dark-haired roommate to sit with you by the window. She checks that the others are comfortable, then joins you.
Dinner becomes a long conversation about little things you have noticed in each other. The city moves quietly beyond the glass.
You admit what you have been hoping to say. She shares her own feelings, leaving room for questions and an unhurried answer.
When you return to the table, home still feels like home. A new connection can begin without anyone having to rush.
You ask whether they would both like to stay and talk. Each answers for herself, and you agree that nobody has to decide more tonight.
You share dinner and explain what you each want, what feels comfortable and what you are still figuring out.
The teasing gives way to a conversation all three of you can take part in. You agree to keep asking rather than assume.
The dishes can wait, and the next choice belongs to all of you. For now, you are happy to stay together.
